The latest Sisley collection is now available on Myntra and includes apparel across categories such as T-shirts, shirts, tops, knitwear, trousers, jeans, skirts, coats, blazers, and jackets for men and women. The launch strengthens Myntra’s presence in the premium fashion and international apparel segment in India.

Sisley was established in Paris in 1968 and became part of the Benetton Group in 1974. The brand has built a global presence across key fashion markets and is now looking to expand its reach among Indian consumers through Myntra’s digital commerce platform.

Venu Nair, SVP, Chief of Strategic Partnerships and Omni-channel, Myntra said, “India has emerged as one of the world's most dynamic fashion markets, and Myntra is uniquely positioned to enable iconic global brands like Sisley to tap into this massive opportunity and strategically scale their presence. The brand brings a distinctive premium contemporary Italian fashion perspective to the fashion-forward Indian shoppers.”

Nicola Capone, CEO, Distribution, Benetton Group said, “The launch of Sisley in India through Myntra represents an important step in strengthening the brand’s presence in a market of strategic relevance. We believe that Indian consumers will appreciate Sisley’s distinctive identity as an urban lifestyle brand, combining creativity, contemporary design, and a unique interpretation of fashion trends. This partnership provides a solid foundation for expanding the brand’s reach and supporting its long-term development in India.”

The launch comes as international fashion brands continue to gain traction in India, with consumers increasingly seeking premium apparel, global fashion trends, and international labels through online retail channels. Myntra currently offers a portfolio of more than 500 international brands on its platform.

Global SS Beauty Brands Limited (GSSBB), a subsidiary of Shoppers Stop Limited, has entered into an exclusive strategic partnership with INTERPARFUMS SA to distribute, develop, and grow its portfolio of prestige fragrance brands in India. The partnership marks a significant move in India's luxury beauty and fragrance market, with GSSBB taking responsibility for the distribution, market development, and brand-building of INTERPARFUMS SA’s fragrance portfolio across the country.

Founded in 1982, INTERPARFUMS SA designs, manufactures, and distributes prestige fragrances and fragrance-related products through licensing and other agreements with international brand owners. The company operates in more than 120 countries and manages fragrance brands including Coach, Montblanc, Jimmy Choo, Lacoste, Rochas, Lanvin, Karl Lagerfeld, and Van Cleef & Arpels.

The collaboration aims to strengthen the presence of global luxury fragrance brands in India, a market witnessing growing demand for premium beauty and personal care products. By combining INTERPARFUMS SA’s international fragrance portfolio with GSSBB’s retail expertise, market insights, and consumer reach, the companies plan to expand their footprint in the Indian luxury fragrance segment.

Philippe Benacin, Co-founder and CEO, INTERPARFUMS SA, said, “India is one of the most promising luxury fragrance markets globally, driven by a young, aspirational consumer base and a growing appreciation for prestigious international brands. At INTERPARFUMS our portfolio is built on decades of craftsmanship, innovation, and enduring brand equity. We are delighted to introduce our brands to Indian consumers with a partner that possesses deep market expertise and a strong understanding of the luxury beauty landscape. Global SS Beauty Brands brings the retail excellence and strategic insight needed to build our brands with purpose, and we look forward to a long-term, successful partnership.”

Biju Kassim, MD and CEO, Global SS Beauty Brands Ltd said, " Our partnership with INTERPARFUMS SA marks another important milestone in our journey to strengthen the luxury fragrance category in India. As consumer demand for globally renowned prestige brands continues to grow, our focus is on building these brands for the long term through thoughtful market development, meaningful consumer engagement, and exceptional retail experiences. INTERPARFUMS' portfolio represents some of the world's most iconic fragrance brands, and we are excited to partner with them to unlock their full potential in India while further reinforcing Global SS Beauty Brands as the partner of choice for leading global beauty brands.”

The agreement is expected to support the expansion of premium fragrance brands in India while strengthening GSSBB’s position in the luxury beauty retail and prestige fragrance categories.

Bhumika Realty, the real estate arm of Bhumika Group, has announced the signing of Lifestyle for a 24,000 sq. ft. anchor store at The Icon, Faridabad, further strengthening the retail mix at its flagship mixed-use development. The new store will span the ground and first floors of the project and is expected to bring one of India’s leading fashion and lifestyle retail destinations to consumers in the city.

Lifestyle, part of the Dubai-based Landmark Group, operates more than 170 stores across eight countries and has established a strong presence in the fashion and lifestyle retail segment. In India, the retailer has a network of over 77 stores across 44 cities, offering customers access to more than 300 international brands across categories including fashion, footwear, beauty, and accessories.

The addition of Lifestyle is expected to enhance the retail offering at The Icon, which is being developed as an integrated destination combining retail, entertainment, hospitality, and residential components.

Uddhav Poddar, CMD, Bhumika Group said, “Faridabad is evolving into an important consumption and retail market within the NCR, with consumers increasingly looking for leading brands and quality experiences closer to home. Bringing Lifestyle to The Icon is an important addition to our retail mix and reinforces our vision of creating a destination that combines leading retail, entertainment and hospitality. Along with PVR INOX, Lifestyle further strengthens the brand ecosystem we are building at The Icon.”

The announcement follows the recent addition of a 25,000 sq. ft. PVR INOX multiplex at the project, strengthening its entertainment component and supporting Bhumika Realty’s strategy of creating a comprehensive lifestyle destination in Faridabad.

The Icon has been designed by Bentel Associates, South Africa. The project is planned as a mixed-use development integrating premium retail spaces, entertainment options, hospitality offerings, and residential units within a single destination.

With the signing of Lifestyle, Bhumika Realty continues to attract prominent retail brands to The Icon, reinforcing Faridabad’s growing importance as a retail and consumption hub within the National Capital Region. The development is expected to cater to rising demand from consumers seeking premium shopping and entertainment experiences closer to their homes.

Pet care platform WAGR is broadening its offerings beyond pet products by bringing together shopping, AI-powered guidance, service discovery, and personalized pet information into a single ecosystem. The move comes as pet ownership in India continues to grow, with consumers increasingly seeking integrated solutions for nutrition, grooming, training, wellness, and healthcare needs.

The company aims to address challenges faced by pet parents who often rely on multiple platforms and service providers to manage different aspects of pet care. By combining products, guidance, and services in one place, WAGR is positioning itself as a comprehensive platform for pet owners.

WAGR currently offers products from established pet care brands including Royal Canin, Pedigree, Whiskas, Sheba, Drools, and Temptations, alongside emerging brands such as Bruni Boi, Cuddl, Cure By Design, Halalicious, Moe Puppy, and Let’s Wag. Its portfolio spans categories including pet food, treats, grooming products, wellness solutions, toys, accessories, and daily essentials for dogs and cats.

The company said its strategy is centered on supporting pet parents throughout their journey rather than focusing solely on product purchases.

Fredun Medhora, Director, WAGR said, “We don’t want WAGR to be another place where pet parents shop; we want it to become a companion they turn to. The opportunity is to bring together products, answers, trusted services and technology around the everyday reality of pet parenting. We are building for that future, even if it means taking bets the category has not taken before.”

As part of this approach, WAGR has introduced TOTO, an AI-powered pet-parenting companion designed to help users navigate everyday concerns related to feeding, nutrition, activity, grooming, behavior, and general pet care. The tool is intended to provide guidance and information, particularly for first-time pet owners, while helping them make more informed decisions. The company clarified that TOTO is not intended to provide veterinary diagnosis, treatment, or replace professional medical advice.

WAGR has also expanded its platform through its Discover feature, which connects pet parents with service providers such as groomers, trainers, walkers, boarding facilities, veterinary clinics, and other pet-care professionals. The initiative is aimed at simplifying the process of finding trusted service providers, a challenge often faced by new pet owners.

In addition, the platform’s Pet Profile feature allows users to maintain important pet information, health records, and other details in one place. According to the company, integrating pet profiles with shopping, guidance, and service discovery enables a more personalized experience for users.

L Catterton has acquired a minority stake in Bengaluru-based restaurant company Nandhana Foods, which operates the Nandhana Palace and RNR brands.

According to media reports, the investment is estimated at around USD 30 million, although the exact deal value and stake size have not been officially disclosed.

Nandhana Foods has built its business around Andhra and Karnataka cuisine and has a presence across Bengaluru and Chennai. The company operates more than 30 locations and was developed under the leadership of Dr. Ravichandar and his daughters Shweta, Ramya and Ravina.

The investment comes as regional restaurant chains continue to attract investor interest amid the expansion of India’s organised food services market. L Catterton said the partnership will support the company’s next phase of growth, with a focus on strengthening operations and expanding into existing and new markets.

“South Indian cuisine is one of the largest segments of India’s burgeoning food services market,” L Catterton said.

The investment firm said the segment is being supported by increasing per-capita spending on dining out and food delivery, along with a rise in consumption occasions. L Catterton also sees scope for Nandhana to expand its presence across South India and enter additional markets.

“We are thrilled to announce the partnership of L Catterton with Nandhana Palace, a legendary culinary institution that has been delighting food lovers across South India for over three decades,” said Sanjiv Mehta, Executive Chairman India, L Catterton, in a LinkedIn post.

The partnership is expected to focus on professionalising the business while retaining its established heritage and values. L Catterton also plans to work with the founding family on scaling operations and expanding the restaurant network.

The transaction adds to the growing investor activity in India’s foodservice sector, particularly around established regional brands with multi-city operations. For Nandhana, the partnership comes at a time when restaurant operators are looking to increase their footprint while building more structured business and operational systems.

Jewellery retailer BlueStone has appointed Amit Jain, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of CarDekho Group, as a Non-Executive Non-Independent Director, effective September 14, 2026.

The appointment was approved during the company’s 15th Annual General Meeting. Jain succeeds Sameer Dileep Nath, who retired by rotation and did not seek reappointment to the board.

Founded in 2011, BlueStone operates as an omnichannel jewellery retailer, combining its online platform with a growing network of physical stores across India. The company offers a wide range of jewellery products and has continued to strengthen its presence in the organised jewellery retail market.

BlueStone describes itself as India’s second-largest digital-first omnichannel jewellery brand. During the first quarter of FY27, the company expanded its retail footprint by opening 12 new stores, taking its total store count to 352 outlets across 139 cities. The brand currently serves customers across more than 12,660 PIN codes, with nearly half of its stores located in Tier II and Tier III cities.

The company also reported strong financial performance during the quarter. In Q1 FY27, BlueStone recorded Rs 737 crore in operating revenue, reflecting a 49 percent year-on-year growth. The jewellery retailer posted a net profit of Rs 6 crore, compared to a net loss of Rs 35 crore during the corresponding period last year, marking a return to profitability.

BlueStone's improving financial performance comes amid continued expansion in India's organised jewellery sector, where it competes with major players including CaratLane, Tanishq, Kalyan Jewellers, Senco Gold, PC Jeweller, and Thangamayil Jewellery.

With Amit Jain joining its board, BlueStone aims to strengthen its leadership team as it continues to scale its omnichannel jewellery business and expand its retail presence across the country.

Samsung India expects its digital appliances business to deliver double-digit year-on-year growth in the second half of 2026, supported by festive season demand and increasing consumer preference for premium home appliances, according to a senior company executive.

Ghufran Alam, Vice President, Digital Appliances Business, Samsung India, said the company has witnessed encouraging sales trends beginning with the Onam season and expects the momentum to continue through upcoming festivals, including Dussehra and Diwali.

The company remains optimistic about consumer spending despite inflationary concerns and global economic uncertainties.

Commenting on market demand, Alam said, "Independence Day sales, which were before the Onam period (August 26), we have seen robust demand. So, Diwali also, and coming festivals also, we see good growth prospects for the appliances business in India."

The Onam season, which traditionally marks the start of India's festive shopping period, delivered strong results for the home appliances sector. Samsung reported high double-digit growth during the period, reflecting sustained consumer interest across product categories.

On pricing, Samsung said it is closely monitoring commodity costs, including copper prices, but has not made any decision regarding price increases ahead of the festive season.

"Whether we are going to increase the price in Diwali or before the festival, we do not have any kind of, at this moment, we do not know currently, because it is all very dynamic," Alam noted.

The company also highlighted the growing trend of premiumisation within India's consumer electronics and home appliances market. Samsung said average selling prices are increasing at a faster pace than overall volumes, indicating stronger demand for premium products across both urban and rural markets. Flexible financing options such as no-cost EMI schemes are also encouraging consumers to upgrade to higher-value products.

Among key categories, room air conditioners (RACs) are expected to remain Samsung's fastest-growing segment during the second half of the year, followed by washing machines and refrigerators. The company attributed this growth to sustained cooling demand in southern India and increased festive purchases.

Within the refrigerator category, Samsung is witnessing stronger demand for French-door and side-by-side refrigerators, particularly models with capacities exceeding 450 litres. In washing machines, consumers are increasingly opting for larger-capacity products ranging between 10 kg and 14 kg across both front-load and top-load segments.

Ahead of the festive season, Samsung has expanded its premium appliance portfolio with the introduction of new air conditioner models, including a cassette AC and a room AC. The company has also upgraded the artificial intelligence capabilities of its Family Hub refrigerators through Gemini integration, enhancing food recognition features beyond the previously supported range.

Amazon has launched Alexa+ in India, introducing a new generative AI-powered version of its voice assistant designed to offer more natural conversations, personalized experiences, and deeper integration with smart home devices, shopping services, entertainment platforms, and daily utility applications. The company said Alexa+ is now available under Early Access at no additional cost for eligible Echo smart speakers, smart displays, Fire TV devices, and the Alexa mobile app. The launch marks Amazon's latest push into the rapidly growing artificial intelligence, smart home, voice technology, and digital assistant segments in India.

Teena Sidana, Country Manager for Alexa, Amazon India said, "Indian households are multi-generational, multilingual, and beautifully complex. Alexa+ was designed for that complexity. She understands intent, adapts to your household’s preferences, and lets each family member interact in the way that feels most natural to them. India is home to one of the most diverse set of customers in the world, and we're excited for them to experience how much smarter, personalized, and more intuitive Alexa+ has become. It was truly built around the way they live. We want to make everyday life simpler for hundreds of millions of people who speak, shop, and live differently from one another and build the world's best personal assistant.”

According to Amazon, Alexa+ has been built to understand conversational speech patterns and user intent, allowing customers to interact naturally without repeatedly using the wake word. The assistant supports English, Hindi, and Hinglish, enabling users to switch languages during conversations while maintaining context.

Amazon said additional Indian language support will be introduced in the future.

Alexa+ is designed to work with a range of connected devices and services used by Indian consumers. The platform supports smart home products from brands including Atomberg, Qubo, Dreame, and Wipro, enabling voice-based control of appliances and connected devices.

Users can also access recipe recommendations through Sanjeev Kapoor Recipes and discover music, podcasts, movies, and TV shows across platforms such as Amazon Music, Spotify, Apple Music, JioSaavn, Prime Video, and Netflix.

Amazon further revealed that integrations with EazyDiner, Swiggy, District by Zomato, MakeMyTrip, Home Triangle, and TripAdvisor will be introduced soon, expanding Alexa+'s capabilities across food delivery, restaurant reservations, travel bookings, home services, and event planning.

The company said Alexa+ uses voice and visual identification technologies to recognize individual family members and tailor responses based on preferences and routines. The assistant can remember dietary preferences, entertainment choices, and daily schedules, allowing it to provide customized recommendations and reminders for different household members.

Amazon has also integrated shopping-focused features into Alexa+, enabling customers to create shopping lists, track Amazon orders, receive price-drop alerts, compare products, summarize verified customer reviews, and discover related products through voice interactions.

The company added that customers will soon be able to order groceries and everyday essentials using voice commands through Amazon Now, completing purchases through natural conversations.

Amazon said Alexa+ has been developed with a strong focus on Indian languages, cultural references, and communication styles. The assistant can understand local expressions, relationship terms, measurements, and commonly used phrases that are part of everyday conversations across Indian households.

The company noted that a significant portion of the technology powering Alexa+'s cultural and linguistic understanding was developed by teams based in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, and Chennai.

Alexa+ is powered by Amazon Bedrock, which connects more than 70 large language models, including Amazon-developed AI models and models from Anthropic. Amazon said the platform automatically selects the most suitable model depending on the task being performed.

The company also highlighted privacy and security features, including access to the Alexa Privacy Dashboard, voice recording controls, microphone and camera settings, and transparency tools that allow customers to review interactions.

Alexa+ is currently available through eligible Echo devices, Fire TV products, and the Alexa app in India. Browser access is expected to be introduced at a later stage.

The service will remain free during the Early Access period. After Early Access concludes, Alexa+ will continue to be available at no additional cost for Prime plan members. For Prime Lite, Prime Shopping Edition, and non-Prime customers, access will be offered through a standalone subscription priced at Rs 2,000 per month or through an eligible Prime membership plan.

Amazon also introduced new Alexa+-optimized devices, including the Echo Show 8, Echo Show 11, Echo Dot Max, and Echo Studio, which have been designed with enhanced processing power and next-generation hardware capabilities.

Real estate major DLF Limited has appointed Nimit Porwal as Vice President, responsible for driving the growth and development of its DLF5 business in Gurugram. Porwal shared the update in a LinkedIn post, saying he was beginning a "new mandate" at a familiar organization and looked forward to contributing to DLF5's continued expansion.

In his new role, he will oversee business strategy, product development, project execution, and profit and loss (P&L) management across DLF5's luxury residential and retail portfolio. The appointment comes as DLF continues to strengthen its presence in India's luxury real estate, premium housing, and retail real estate segments.

Prior to joining DLF, Porwal served as Strategy and P&L Lead for Indore at Godrej Properties, where he led the company's entry into the city. His responsibilities included land acquisitions, project planning, residential project launches, office and team setup, along with sales and marketing operations. Porwal is no stranger to DLF. He previously spent nearly two years with the company as Cluster Business Head, leading business strategy, product management, and P&L operations for the DLF5 super-luxury portfolio.

During his earlier tenure, he led the conceptualization and launch of The Dahlias, a luxury residential project that generated topline revenue of more than Rs 30,000 crore. He also contributed to DLF5's master planning initiatives and played a role in the development strategy for projects such as The Grove and The Summit Plaza.

With experience across real estate development, asset management, investment risk management, and consulting, Porwal has also worked with CBRE India, Piramal Capital and Housing Finance, and KPMG India. The leadership appointment is expected to support DLF's ongoing focus on expanding its luxury residential, mixed-use, and retail real estate portfolio in Gurugram, a key market for the company's long-term growth strategy.

Tata Group-backed jewellery retailer CaratLane has launched a dedicated e-commerce platform for Australia, marking the company's latest step in expanding its international presence. The new website will allow customers across Australia to browse and purchase CaratLane's diamond and gold jewellery collections directly through a localized online platform.

The launch is aimed at improving accessibility for customers in Australia, particularly the Indian diaspora, while strengthening CaratLane's growing global jewellery business. The platform offers a localized shopping experience, including product discovery, online transactions, and nationwide delivery services.

Saumen Bhaumik, Managing Director, CaratLane said, “Indian consumers in Australia have long shown a strong desire for CaratLane designs, making this launch a natural progression for the brand. By introducing a localised platform, we’re removing cross-border friction to deliver a seamless shopping experience directly to their doorsteps, marking a major milestone in our global growth story. It’s part of our larger vision to make CaratLane the most loved jewellery brand amongst Indian women, and Australia plays a critical role in that journey.”

The Australia launch expands CaratLane's international footprint beyond its existing operations in markets including the United States, Canada, Singapore, and the United Kingdom. The company currently serves customers in more than 30 countries and has been increasing its focus on overseas growth through a mix of online and offline channels.

CaratLane has also been strengthening its retail network and omnichannel strategy in India. The jewellery retailer recently outlined plans to add new stores across multiple markets while continuing investments in digital capabilities and customer experience initiatives.

The Australia-focused platform will offer certified jewellery products supported by insured shipping and authenticity documentation. The move reflects the growing trend among Indian jewellery brands to expand internationally through digital commerce, targeting overseas consumers seeking access to Indian-designed jewellery and diamond collections. As global demand for Indian jewellery continues to rise, CaratLane's latest expansion underscores the increasing role of cross-border e-commerce and omnichannel retail strategies in driving growth for Indian jewellery brands.

EBG Group has announced its entry into India’s toy retail and children’s lifestyle market with the launch of Adhira and Appa Toys, a new homegrown toy brand focused on play, learning, and family experiences. The company plans to open its first retail store in Hyderabad by the end of 2026 and invest more than Rs 50 crore to expand the brand to 50 stores across India by 2027.

The brand will offer a wide range of products designed for children from infancy to pre-teen years, spanning categories such as STEM toys, educational toys, robotics kits, science kits, sensory-development products, puzzles, board games, arts and crafts, pretend-play toys, dolls, action figures, ride-ons, plush toys, outdoor play products, electronics, and collectibles.

Irfan Khan, Founder and Chairman, EBG Group said, “We are not building another toy store. We are building a world where children can explore, imagine, learn, and dream. For us, a good toy should create joy today, curiosity tomorrow, and memories that stay with a child for years. The first portfolio features 1,335 products for children from infancy through the pre-teen years. Parents will be able to choose from STEM and educational toys, construction and building sets, robotics and science kits, sensory-development toys, puzzles and board games, arts and crafts, pretend-play products, dolls and action figures, remote-control vehicles, ride-ons and tricycles, plush toys, outdoor play products, electronics and collectibles.”

The launch comes as India's toy manufacturing sector continues to gain momentum under the Government of India's Vocal for Local and Made in India initiatives. Adhira and Appa Toys said it is working with domestic manufacturing partners to develop products for Indian consumers while supporting local production capabilities.

According to government data, India became a net exporter of toys in FY 2025-26, with toy imports declining by 37.5 percent and toy exports increasing by 89.1 percent. Indian-made toys are being exported to markets including the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, and the Netherlands, reflecting growing international demand for products manufactured in India.

The company's strategy aligns with the broader growth outlook for the toy industry. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has previously encouraged Indian toy manufacturers to target opportunities beyond the projected $5 billion Indian toy market by 2034 and capture a larger share of the projected $179 billion global toy market by 2032.

Beyond retail expansion, Adhira and Appa Toys plans to integrate sustainability measures into its operations. The company will focus on domestic and regional sourcing, explore recyclable and reusable packaging solutions, reduce inventory-related wastage, and adopt energy-efficient practices where feasible.

Hari Haran Chandrasekharan, who leads the Adhira and Appa Toys vertical within EBG Group, highlighted sustainability and local sourcing as key focus areas supporting both operational efficiency and Indian manufacturing. The company also plans to expand beyond traditional toy retailing through Adhira and Appa Game Zones, experiential play areas, creative workshops, children's merchandise, gifting solutions, and parent-child engagement formats. An omnichannel platform is also under development to connect online and offline customer experiences.

EBG Group said its first Hyderabad store will serve as a pilot location to understand customer preferences and refine operational processes before scaling across major metropolitan markets and high-growth Tier I and Tier II cities. Future expansion will include flagship stores, mall-based formats, compact stores, and shop-in-shop models. As part of its domestic manufacturing strategy, Adhira and Appa Toys is collaborating with Aditi Toys, a Rajkot-based toy manufacturer, to strengthen local production capabilities and support India's growing toy ecosystem.

Shares in Swedish microcap stock Nanexa more than doubled early Friday after the drug-delivery group revealed a $1.33 billion licensing deal with pharma giant Novo Nordisk .

Nanexa, which trades on the Nasdaq First North Growth Market in Stockholm, said after the closing bell on Thursday it had penned a global licensing agreement covering Novo's long-acting injectable drugs for obesity, type 2 diabetes and other cardiometabolic issues.

Its shares soared more than 150% at the open in Stockholm before settling back to a gain of around 114% by 11:50 a.m. local time. It leaves the stock roughly 12% short of its all-time high in November 2015.

The deal grants Eli Lilly competitor Novo, which makes Wegovy and Ozempic, exclusive rights for up to five development programs to use Nanexa's PharmaShell tech, which applies an ultra-thin inorganic coating on drug particles to control their release over time.

The groups are targeting monthly and quarterly administration of the drugs.

Nanexa is eligible to receive an upfront payment worth around $700 million and potential milestone payments for development and regulatory achievements. The agreement provides for low single-digit royalties on future product sales.

The group reported full-year revenues of approximately $3.89 million for 2025, representing a 48.4% increase on the previous year.

"With this agreement, Nanexa enters a new era of considerable financial strength, allowing us to significantly expand applications of our unique [atomic layer deposition] technology to other therapeutic areas and giving us an opportunity to build a sustainable long-term business," said Nanexa chair Göran Ando.

David Westburg, Nanexa CEO, said the agreement "provides a strong foundation for expanding PharmaShell into additional therapeutic areas and to selectively advance additional internal programs towards clinical proof of concept, allowing us to capture greater value from the breadth of the PharmaShell platform."

text:
Ahead of its upcoming merger with Supernus, Indivior Pharmaceuticals has ended its long-running collaboration with Addex Therapeutics to develop positive allosteric modulators (PAMs).

Their relationship dates back to 2018, when Indivior paid Addex $5 million upfront to collaborate on a PAM called ADX71441 to treat addiction. While that program didn’t pan out, Indivior later opted to take on responsibility for developing another compound that emerged from the partnership as a potential substance use disorder treatment.

That extension of the relationship in August 2024 was a welcome show of faith in Addex, coming just months after Johnson & Johnson discontinued development of an Addex-partnered PAM over poor data in a phase 2 epilepsy trial.

Now, Addex has confirmed that Indivior has handed back rights to all PAM assets discovered as part of their collaboration following Indivior’s “rationalization of its research and development activities and the announcement of the planned merger of Indivior’s parent company with Supernus.”

Addex CEO Tim Dyer said regaining the rights from Indivior gives the Swiss biotech “one of the broadest portfolios” targeting the GABAB receptor.

“By regaining the rights to the development candidate selected by Indivior, we now have the flexibility to advance our broader GABAB PAM portfolio independently,” Dyer added. “This includes the returned candidate for substance use disorders and our proprietary candidate in development for chronic cough.”

“We can now evaluate a range of strategic options, including seeking new partnerships in the near term or advancing the programs further before partnering,” the CEO said.

Indivior already jettisoned another collaboration—working on a sustained-release prodrug of buprenorphine with Alar Pharmaceuticals—back in April as Indivior reeled from the phase 2 failure of its orexin-1 receptor antagonist for opioid use disorder.

text:
The AI data center build-out has turned Nvidia (NVDA) into a $5 trillion company, is helping to power Intel's (INTC) turnaround efforts, and made memory chip makers some of the hottest companies on Earth.

But a growing number of Americans see the boom as a burden being forced upon them that is gobbling up land, power, and water. Coupled with non-disclosure agreements that some companies require towns to sign, the situation has become volatile.

An increasing number of states have introduced legislation halting or banning the construction of data centers, with New York issuing a state-wide, one-year moratorium. Texas has similarly blocked new data center projects until the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) completes an audit to assess the facilities' impact on Texas's power grid and water resources.to halt or ban the construction of data centers, with New York issuing a statewide

To address the matter, Microsoft (MSFT) is taking a more open approach to its data center plans. In March, the company announced it was ending the use of non-disclosure agreements and terminating existing ones.

"At the end of the day, I think we have to get permission from the communities," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella told Deirdre Bosa. "If you are going to be building a data center, consuming power, using water, at the end of the day, we have to earn that permission."

The move is part of what Microsoft calls its Community-First AI Infrastructure Plan. Unveiled in January, the effort includes the software giant paying to ensure electricity rates in data-center areas don't rise, minimizing and replenishing more water than the company uses, hiring local workers, not asking communities to reduce taxes on data centers, and investing in AI training.

"We have a set of commitments, right? I don't think of anything that we do as building a data center and getting out. No. It's about being able to be welcomed in the community on an ongoing basis," Nadella explained.

The CEO pointed to Microsoft's efforts in Quincy, Wash., as an example of how the company says it can move forward. Since Microsoft began constructing its first company-owned data center in 2006, Quincy's poverty rate has declined from 29.4% to 13.1% between 2012 and 2023.

Tax rates for residents have also declined, while the improved tax base has helped pay for a new hospital and other municipal facilities, according to Microsoft.

"They have a new hospital, they have a new school. They have a new city center. And over the years, we've also created a lot of employment opportunities. We have close to a thousand people there," Nadella said.

text:
Accor, Hilton and IHG launched AI discovery tools in 2026.

Booking commissions typically range from 15–30 percent.

Third-party platforms drove most independent hotel bookings in 2025.

ACCOR'S ALL CONCIERGE is the latest example of how hotel owners, franchisees and corporate leadership are using artificial intelligence to put more focus on how guests find and book stays. The way AI mediates that discovery is becoming a distribution-strategy question, alongside OTA commissions, brand-technology fees and guest-acquisition spend.

Accor’s new AI-powered conversational tool, which the company moved from pilot to full-scale rollout this month, guides guests from initial travel inspiration through booking and post-stay support, according to Accor. Hilton and IHG also introduced comparable tools of their own this year, positioning conversational AI as a competitive front across the industry rather than a single company's experiment.

Accor's conversational approach

Accor advances AI with ALL Concierge, a conversational travel companion deployed at scale.Photo credit: Accor

ALL Concierge processed more than 1 million guest conversations since its pilot began in July 2025, insights the company said it used to refine the platform ahead of this wider launch. The tool is available across ALL.com, the ALL Accor app, WhatsApp and iMessage, supporting 11 languages on the website and four languages across five points of sale on mobile, with broader coverage planned by year-end.

“Every great concierge remembers your name and anticipates what you need before you ask,” said Alix Boulnois, Accor's chief commercial, digital and tech officer. “For decades, that level of attention was the privilege of a few. Today, we are making it available to every guest, everywhere, at any hour. And yet, behind every exceptional stay, there will always be a person who cares.”

Our teams are the heart of Accor. What changes today is that they will have a companion just as tireless and attentive, freeing them to focus on what no technology will ever replicate: the human connection that makes hospitality truly memorable.”

Accor has not disclosed adoption figures for the wider rollout. Whether the tool measurably shifts booking behavior away from third-party platforms will depend on guest uptake over time, according to the phased rollout timeline Accor outlined in its announcement.

Boulnois said that Accor's hotel teams remain central to the guest experience even as the tool takes on more of the conversation, adding that support staff can step in whenever a request needs a human touch.

Hilton and IHG are moving in parallel

In March, Hilton launched its AI Planner for curated travel discovery.Photo credit: Hilton Worldwide Holdings

Hilton introduced its own generative AI-powered digital concierge, the Hilton AI Planner, in March, initially in beta to a limited share of hilton.com traffic before expanding, according to Hilton's press release announcing the tool. The tool helps travelers identify destinations, compare properties and explore amenities through conversational search, per the release.

"The launch of the Hilton AI Planner marks another step forward in our journey to reimagine the travel experience for Hilton guests," said Michael Leidinger, Hilton's senior vice president and chief information officer.

IHG Hotels & Resorts launched a beta version of AI-powered conversational search on IHG.com and the IHG One Rewards app in July, the company said. The tool is designed in part to help hotel owners increase their properties' visibility in AI-driven searches, and that it plans to roll out an AI-optimized hotel content platform over the coming months to help owners' properties surface more effectively.

"With these capabilities in place, and more to follow, we are very well positioned to harness the power of AI at scale and deliver rich, inspiring and seamless travel experiences that delight our guests and deliver benefits to our hotel owners," said Elie Maalouf, IHG's chief executive officer, according to the company's release.

Accor also introduced The Butler, a separate AI tool built for hotel staff that provides guidance and information and connects employees with human experts when needed, according to Accor's announcement.

Why it matters to hotel owners and franchisees

OTAs typically charge hotels 15 percent to 30 percent commissions per booking.Photo credit: Istock

The scope of the shift is larger than any single brand's tool, according to Longwoods International's traveler research. The study found that among U.S. travelers who used AI to plan a trip, 54 percent used it to find attractions and activities, 44 percent for travel inspiration and 42 percent for dining options — the same early-journey stages that OTAs and general search engines have historically captured before a guest reaches a hotel brand's own channels, per the study.

Online travel agencies have charged hotel owners commissions typically ranging from 15 percent to 30 percent per booking, depending on the platform, region and partner tier, according to rate disclosures across major OTAs. A 2026 industry report tracking approximately 90 million bookings found that OTAs sourced about 63 percent of independent hotel reservations in 2025, with the share reaching closer to 80 percent in some markets, according to Cloudbeds' State of Independent Hotels report.

For owners and franchisees, that puts AI-native discovery closer to the center of distribution economics rather than at the periphery. A brand's ability to capture guests earlier in the journey — and retain the resulting guest data — can affect guest-acquisition costs and loyalty-program value over time, though the effect will vary by brand, market and how quickly travelers shift habits away from established OTA use.

That raises practical questions for owners and multi-brand operators evaluating brand agreements: how these tools are funded within brand-technology fees, whether participation is mandatory or optional across a portfolio, and what data or reporting owners will receive on whether the tools are actually reducing OTA dependency rather than simply adding a new guest-facing feature.

IHG said its intent to help owners' properties surface more prominently in AI search results, but neither Accor, Hilton nor IHG has yet published data quantifying a shift in booking share away from third-party platforms.

That does not mean AI concierges automatically lower distribution costs. All three tools remain in partial or phased rollout, according to each company's own announcement, and the broader shift toward AI-mediated trip planning could just as easily create a new dependency — on AI platforms rather than OTAs — if hotel brands need visibility inside third-party AI tools to be discovered at all.

text:
A Partnership Built Over Nearly a Century

Air Liquide, a global leader in gases, technologies and services for industry and healthcare, serves more than 4.3 million customers and patients across 59 countries with approximately 65,000 employees worldwide. In Malaysia, the company’s presence dates back to 1927 with the establishment of Far East Oxygen. The business re-established its operations as Air Liquide Malaysia (ALM) in 2007 and continued to expand through the acquisitions of PolyGas in 2016 and Southern Industrial Gas (SIG) in 2019, reflecting its long-standing commitment to the country’s industrial development.

Nearly a century after establishing its first presence in Malaysia, Air Liquide has evolved alongside the country’s industrial transformation. Today, ALM and SIG support more than 2,100 customers through a nationwide network spanning eight key economic states, with eight cylinder-filling centres and two air separation units.

Backed by a workforce of more than 700 local employees and a regional Business Shared Services Hub in Kuala Lumpur, Air Liquide serves a broad range of industries, including semiconductors and electrical and electronics (E&E), advanced materials and engineering, automotive and fabrication, energy, food and beverages, and healthcare.

Beyond supplying industrial gases, Air Liquide delivers integrated solutions that enhance manufacturers’ productivity, reliability, and sustainability. Its portfolio includes ultra-high-purity and specialty gases, on-site supply systems and digital solutions designed to strengthen operational efficiency, process reliability, and safety. Through the Group’s expertise in carbon capture, low-carbon hydrogen and electrolysis, Air Liquide is also supporting manufacturers in their decarbonisation journey, helping them reduce emissions while scaling operations more sustainably.

Why Malaysia: A Platform for Long-Term Growth

For long-term investors, Malaysia’s appeal lies in the strength of its integrated value propositions: a mature manufacturing ecosystem, well-connected supply chains, strategic access to ASEAN, a highly-skilled technical workforce, and policy frameworks that support higher-value, technology-driven, and sustainable growth. National initiatives such as the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 (NIMP 2030), National Semiconductor Strategy (NSS) and National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) provide a clear and consistent direction for industrial transformation, reinforcing the country’s position as a top destination for advanced manufacturing and future-ready industries.

These advantages have enabled companies such as Air Liquide to grow alongside Malaysia’s industrial evolution. As the country’s semiconductor and E&E sectors continue to expand, demand is rising for dependable, high-purity industrial gases and advanced process solutions that support increasingly sophisticated manufacturing. Reflecting its long-term confidence in Malaysia, Air Liquide has invested more than RM650 million in the country and continues to strengthen its local capabilities to support the next phase of industrial growth and reinforce the resilience of Malaysia’s manufacturing ecosystem.

This long-standing partnership is further strengthened through MIDA’s investment facilitation role. Beyond supporting Air Liquide’s expansion, MIDA works closely with investors across the investment lifecycle, from project implementation and relevant stakeholder coordination to aligning with national industrial priorities. Through this coordinated ecosystem, businesses are better supported to establish, expand and innovate in Malaysia.

Malaysia’s sustainability ambitions also complement Air Liquide’s long-term strategy. At Group level, Air Liquide reported that its 2025 carbon intensity was 46% below its 2015 level, exceeding its 30% reduction target, as it progresses towards carbon neutrality across its value chain by 2050. This shared commitment to sustainable industrial growth reinforces Malaysia’s attractiveness as a destination for companies seeking to balance competitiveness with responsible business practices.

The upgraded facility delivers tangible improvements across three areas:

Quality and Precision: Pre-set digital “recipes” coordinate cryogenic pumps and valve sequences, ensuring consistent gas purity, while reducing process variation.

Safer Operations: Automated control of high-pressure valve sequences and frequency-controlled cryogenic pumps reduces operator exposure and reinforces Air Liquide’s ‘Safety First’ culture.

Reliability and Scale: Specialised skid configurations double production throughput while minimising downtime, enabling a faster and more reliable response to growing customer demand.

Beyond enhancing operational performance, the Bukit Minyak expansion reflects how continuous investment in technology and innovation strengthens Malaysia’s industrial capabilities. By improving productivity, operational resilience, and the supply of critical industrial gases, the facility supports the evolving needs of Malaysia’s high-value manufacturing sectors, particularly semiconductors, E&E, and other advanced industries.

As Malaysia continues to attract more high-value investments in semiconductors, computing infrastructure ecosystem, advanced manufacturing, and the digital economy, companies like Air Liquide will play an increasingly important role in enabling these industries through specialised technologies and reliable industrial solutions. Nearly a century after establishing its presence in Malaysia, the company’s continued expansion reflects a broader story of investor confidence – one built on Malaysia’s mature industrial ecosystem, highly skilled workforce, and long-term commitment to innovation and sustainable growth.

To learn more about Air Liquide Malaysia Sdn. Bhd., visit https://my.airliquide.com/.

name: Ecolab
title: From ambition to action: Operationalizing water circularity as a strategic growth asset
description:
The historical model of industrial water management - built on a linear "Take-Use-Discharge" framework - is rapidly colliding with physical and economic limits.
Because reliable water access underpins approximately 60% of global GDP, industrial operators must undergo a fundamental paradigm shift: treating water infrastructure as a core, strategic growth asset that directly impacts operational throughput, product quality, and long-term business resilience.
To successfully move from ambition to action, forward-thinking operators are abandoning fragmented, isolated water treatments in favor of an integrated, closed-loop approach.
Standardizing excellence: Shifting the benchmarking paradigm The first major hurdle in transitioning to a circular water model is internal perception.
When a facility can quantify its water efficiency gap relative to best-in-class operators, water circularity transforms from a vague environmental aspiration into a clear, justifiable engineering project.
text:
Corporate sustainability has reached an inflection point. Globally, industrial enterprises have spent the past several years announcing ambitious commitments to achieve net-zero carbon emissions, water neutrality, and watershed resilience. Yet, as operations managers and water professionals know all too well, there remains a significant gap between high-level executive commitments and actual execution.

The historical model of industrial water management - built on a linear "Take-Use-Discharge" framework - is rapidly colliding with physical and economic limits. With a projected 56% global freshwater shortfall looming by 2030, water can no longer be viewed as a cheap, infinite commodity or a static utility cost.

Because reliable water access underpins approximately 60% of global GDP, industrial operators must undergo a fundamental paradigm shift: treating water infrastructure as a core, strategic growth asset that directly impacts operational throughput, product quality, and long-term business resilience.

To successfully move from ambition to action, forward-thinking operators are abandoning fragmented, isolated water treatments in favor of an integrated, closed-loop approach. This transition requires a dual-focus playbook: standardizing performance through rigorous benchmarking and engineering outcome-driven operations to drive economic results.

Standardizing excellence: Shifting the benchmarking paradigm

The first major hurdle in transitioning to a circular water model is internal perception. Traditionally, wastewater treatment and effluent compliance have been managed as risk-mitigation cost centers. To reframe water as a strategic asset, organizations must establish a baseline of operational transparency that connects facility data directly to enterprise value.

This is where standardizing excellence through verified benchmarking becomes indispensable. By leveraging established disclosure frameworks and implementing performance metrics like Ecolab and CDP’s Water Use Efficiency Index, industrial operators can objectively evaluate their water performance against global industry peers.

Rather than viewing these indices as simple compliance exercises, advanced facilities utilize them to identify hidden inefficiencies across their unit operations, build a scalable data-backed roadmap, and justify capital deployment for circular water infrastructure. When a facility can quantify its water efficiency gap relative to best-in-class operators, water circularity transforms from a vague environmental aspiration into a clear, justifiable engineering project.

Engineering to outcomes: Navigating interdependencies

Once an organization establishes its baseline, the challenge shifts to physical execution. The primary reason many circular water initiatives stall is a failure to recognize operational interdependencies. An industrial facility is a web of connected thermal and chemical systems; a water treatment decision made at a cooling tower inevitably cascades down to impact heat exchangers, boiler feedwater networks, and wastewater treatment plants.

Taking a purely siloed approach to these units introduces hidden cost drivers and operational risks. True value capture requires an integrated, programmatic systems approach. By conducting comprehensive front-end mapping and a total water-and-energy balance, engineers can design systems that treat distinct wastewater streams independently based on their specific chemical profiles, preparing them for recycling.

This level of circularity helps effluent water to be systematically reclaimed and returned back into operations, maximizing throughput while minimizing raw water intake and discharge fees.

Real-world execution: The circular blueprint in industry

The tangible commercial viability of this programmatic approach is best demonstrated within heavy manufacturing, where extreme water quality and reliable volumes directly dictate product yield.

Consider a steel refining facility in France that produces approximately 700 kilotons of color-coated steel coils for modern architecture annually. To manufacture a premium product, the plant requires an uncompromised supply of high-purity water. Facing an aging pretreatment infrastructure, the facility partnered with Ecolab to execute a comprehensive Total Water Management solution that optimized the site's entire water ecosystem.

The engineering solution integrated a centralized, automated demineralization plant -deployed in four modular, containerized units - with real-time 3D TRASAR™ monitoring and advanced analytics. Concurrently, the facility's existing effluent recycling unit was upgraded, and a specialized chemical dosing platform was introduced to maximize site-wide chemical safety.

By systematically managing the plant's water interdependencies, the facility successfully operationalized its sustainability goals into distinct commercial milestones. The state-of-the-art system consistently maintains the required 70 cubic meters of demineralized water per hour production rate, ensuring maximum manufacturing throughput.

Simultaneously, the upgraded recycling system cut the facility's raw water expenditure by $80,000 per year and eliminated $180,000 of acrylate waste discharge annually. Combined with optimized operational efficiencies and enhanced on-site chemical safety, this programmatic circular design delivers $500,000 in total financial savings to the enterprise every year.

Conclusion: Securing the license to operate

The lessons learned from this example are clear: water circularity is not an operational liability or an expensive compliance burden. When engineered through a programmatic framework that links advanced chemistry, automation, and real-time digital intelligence, water circularity becomes a powerful engine for cost control and productivity.

As local regulations intensify and global freshwater scarcity escalates, the industries that survive and thrive will be those that move past high-level discussion. By implementing a rigorous, data-driven blueprint that treats wastewater as a premium asset rather than a disposable byproduct, forward-thinking operators are successfully securing their future license to operate - decoupling their industrial growth from resource consumption while delivering profound value to the enterprise and the surrounding community alike.

text:
After racking up a trio of regulatory wins overseas, Eli Lilly’s once-weekly insulin is coming home to open a new front in the company’s ongoing market showdown with Novo.

The FDA has signed off on Lilly’s Onswik, also known as insulin efsitora alfa-gobe, as a new once-weekly basal insulin to help keep blood sugar in check in patients with type 2 diabetes.

With the green light, Lilly will now be able to introduce a direct competitor to Novo’s Awiqli in the U.S.

Approved in late March, Awiqli, Novo’s own solution to daily basal insulin shots, has managed to eke out a commercial head start over Lilly’s drug, in a dynamic that echoes the rollout of the companies’ oral obesity medications earlier this year.

Meanwhile, the new FDA go-ahead marks Onswik’s fourth global regulatory win, following actions from regulators in the European Union, Mexico and Japan.

The FDA’s decision leveraged data from Lilly’s late-stage Qwint program, which looked at Onswik in more than 3,400 patients with type 2 diabetes. In each trial, the drug met the primary endpoint of noninferior A1C reduction from baseline compared with insulin glargine or insulin degludec.

Breaking things down, Onswik helped curb patients’ A1C by 1.31% versus 1.27% for insulin glargine at 52 weeks in Qwint-1, which looked at patients with type 2 diabetes using insulin for the first time. The drug reduced A1C by 0.86% at week 26 in Qwint-3 and 1.07% over that same span in Qwint-4, compared with 0.75% for insulin degludec and 1.07% for insulin glargine, respectively.

Qwint-3 assessed patients who had previously used basal insulin, while the fourth Qwint study looked at those who had previously used daily basal insulin and mealtime insulin. Qwint-2, meanwhile, stratified insulin-naive patients based on whether they were also using a GLP-1 receptor agonist. Onswik was noninferior to insulin degludec regardless of GLP-1 use.

By 2030, more than 510 million people around the world are expected to be living with diabetes, mainly in the form of type 2 disease, and some 37 million are expected to use insulin, according to Lilly.

"For over a century, Lilly has been developing insulins that transformed diabetes care for millions of people worldwide, but delays in initiating treatment and the burden of daily injections can have a real impact on patients' day-to-day experience managing type 2 diabetes," said Kenneth Custer, Ph.D., Lilly’s EVP and president of cardiometabolic health, in a statement.

With an approval in hand, Lilly says it plans to launch Onswik in the U.S. “in the coming months.” The company is rolling out the product in 500 units/mL and 1,000 units/mL concentrations.

As Lilly gets its ducks in a row for the Onswik launch, Novo is now coming up on the second month of Awiqli’s U.S. market run. The Danish drugmaker debuted its weekly insulin on Aug. 11.

While insulin remains a key backbone of both Lilly’s and Novo’s businesses, and a reminder of the metabolic medicine makers’ long histories addressing diabetes, the companies’ GLP-1 medicines have stolen center stage in recent years, particularly in their blockbuster obesity indications.

title: Microsoft unveils Copilot super app, targeting business users with AI agents | Fortune
description:
The super app is a major redesign of Microsoft’s existing Copilot app, bringing together a variety of features and capabilities intended to create a Swiss Army knife for AI productivity.

Microsoft’s super app reveal also follows a stretch of growing pains for Copilot.
text:
Microsoft is launching its super app as a central interface through which customers can chat with AI bots, tap AI tools to help accomplish tasks, write code, and access a new “Autopilot” feature that brings agentic capabilities — AI that can act on tasks on its own — to the company’s flagship AI app. The super app is a major redesign of Microsoft’s existing Copilot app, bringing together a variety of features and capabilities intended to create a Swiss Army knife for AI productivity. The launch follows a push by Microsoft to merge what had become a sprawling collection of Copilot products that critics said left customers confused.

For Chief Executive Satya Nadella, the new Copilot is a way to win subscriptions in a business that’s become increasingly important to the software maker, while also ensuring that Microsoft’s lucrative productivity offerings don’t get sidelined by a new generation of AI rivals.

The super app, first reported by Fortune in May, also plugs into Microsoft’s Office tools, letting users ask a bot to handle a task on an Excel spreadsheet or change a layout in a Word document. Though there is a free version of the super app, customers will need their Microsoft subscriptions or workplace licenses to unlock its full range of offerings. Both enterprise customers and individual users will have to pay extra based on usage of its most autonomous capabilities.

“We do want this to become an all-in-one productivity suite,” Annie Pearl, corporate vice president of Copilot, told Fortune. That includes being a platform “where you can ask questions, you could delegate complex multi-step work, you can build software for internal and external use cases, and you can automate tasks through your kind of digital worker or personal agent.”

The Autopilot feature lets users name their agent, assign it a role and a goal, then set it loose on tasks such as project updates, tracking work decisions and deadlines, reminding colleagues when commitments are due, gathering prep materials, and reaching out to partners.

The coding feature targets non-software engineers who want to build apps, a dashboard, or other tools and platforms, Pearl said, though she added that it will grow more powerful over time.

Most of the app’s new features are rolling out through an early-test program, and Microsoft has not set a timeline for general availability. The coding tool, which shares its underlying tech stack with Microsoft’s GitHub Copilot, will reach Microsoft 365 Premium and Pro subscribers through the test program later this year. Autopilot will undergo a more restricted phase of user testing, and broad rollout will hinge on how testers rate the new tools.

Competitive pressure

Microsoft is betting the super app will supercharge its Copilot brand by using AI directly connected to the business tools that already make it money. As OpenAI and Anthropic push into enterprise offerings, Microsoft is racing to protect its turf and keep pace with customer expectations. It’s also launching the app just as agentic capabilities break into the mainstream. OpenAI unveiled its own super app in July. Meta Platforms has already seen early success with its new Muse app, which targets general consumers, letting them create a personal agent to handle food orders, bank statements, and other tasks.

Microsoft’s super app reveal also follows a stretch of growing pains for Copilot. Nadella has shaken up executive ranks to position the company competitively against the top AI labs and enterprise rivals, forging a unified Copilot team earlier this year that merged the consumer and enterprise sides under Jacob Andreou, the fast-rising executive now in charge of Copilot.

Copilot stumbled early, plagued by branding issues, limited capabilities, and Microsoft’s decision to launch several versions of the AI that confused customers. Its consumer Copilot failed to reach mainstream success. More recently, as Microsoft has refocused on enterprise and streamlined its operations, it’s found some traction. In July, the company said its Microsoft 365 Copilot had surpassed 30 million paid seats, with net seats added doubling quarter over quarter. Its shares have rebounded over the past six months on the strength of its cloud computing business, fueled by AI demand and Copilot growth.

Security concerns

Copilot relies mostly on models from Anthropic and OpenAI, though it also accesses xAI’s Grok models, Pearl said. Security has also been a top concern, especially as models from OpenAI and Anthropic have been used to hack into other companies in recent months, stoking worldwide unease about AI capabilities. On Wednesday, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent infiltrated an Australian government website in June, marking the latest such incident.

Microsoft said it has built several safety guards into its app. Those include rules requiring its Autopilot agents to carry explicit permissions, full audit logs, and tracking. Humans decide how much autonomy an agent receives, the company said. When non-developers build apps using the Code tool, the software runs tasks in isolated local or cloud-hosted environments, with controls intended to protect customer data and systems.

“Everything that you observe should be governable by policy,” Nadella told customers this week at a presentation at Microsoft’s Redmond, Wash. headquarters. “That’s the classic thing we have done for decades when it comes to IT management, and now I need to do that with every agent out there.

“The way we have conceptualized Copilot is to think of this not as just any one product or one form factor, but as a system that brings form and function together.”

Microsoft also plans to monetize the new features by charging extra for its best capabilities. Seats paid for by enterprise customers or individual users cover “everyday AI” such as Chat, Office integration, and standard routing, while usage-based billing can apply to Code, Autopilot, and access to the newest, most capable AI models.

Microsoft also plans future add-ons that would tie in even more of its ecosystem. That includes a function called “Today,” which Microsoft says will integrate emails, calendar, Teams, and tasks to organize and prioritize workloads. It will actively complete tasks, such as generating drafts, proposing schedule updates, and setting up follow-ups for quick user action, the company said.

text:
OpenAI's ChatGPT is still the face of consumer AI. But it's no longer the hot new thing.

Meta's Muse agent overtook ChatGPT on the free app charts this week, part of a new craze over personal AI assistants in Silicon Valley. Muse can browse, click, type, and chat across the internet, handling tasks you give it. Meta is adding Muse to its smart glasses and building a new Tamagotchi-esque gadget called Muse Charm, it announced at its Connect conference on Wednesday.

The capabilities aren't new; ChatGPT can do many of the same things. At the same time, Muse's explosive growth is still a major headache for OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

Muse proves that an AI tool can handle work without relying on OpenAI's frontier models. It shows that Meta will pour huge amounts of money into keeping a ChatGPT competitor free. And it signals that OpenAI's longtime push into "browser use" — one of the capabilities that Muse rests on — isn't turning into a moat.

OpenAI hasn't launched a direct answer to Muse, though it could easily do so at its DevDay conference on Tuesday.

As early adopters suss out new AI assistant options, OpenAI risks getting left behind. There's Instinct, from a tiny startup run by a 23-year-old. There's SpaceXAI's Grok Bot and Google's Gemini Spark, with all the firepower of those giant companies. And then there's Muse, bolstered by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's aggressive growth tactics.

The internet has begun rumbling about rumors of a competitor from OpenAI. And Thibault Sottiaux, an OpenAI product leader, teased a release. He replied to a post about agents, showing notifications from Muse, Instinct, and Grok Bot and saying "it's enough," with a hand-wave emoji.

"Everyone is sort of circling around this," Techsponential analyst Avi Greengart told Business Insider.

He said each assistant launch fits a general trend from the companies: they're "all trying to arrive at a durable and monetizable way to use AI to, hopefully, improve people's lives."

Meta's apps dominate for consumers

OpenAI's chief rival has always been Anthropic, and all the while, OpenAI owned a major advantage: ChatGPT is way bigger than Claude. OpenAI's tool hit 1 billion weekly active users this year.

Against Meta, that brag won't fly. Zuckerberg's empire extends to more than 3 billion daily active users across Instagram, Facebook, Messenger, and WhatsApp. It's easy for Meta to promote a new tool to vast numbers of users, plus the company's advertising business prints enough cash to fund billions in AI compute. Meta's smart glasses have also turned into a hit, giving it another touchpoint for the Muse assistant.

More than 2.5 million people downloaded Muse on mobile in the 13 days after its launch, according to Sensor Tower, a market intelligence firm.

Seema Shah, vice president of insights at the firm, told Business Insider she sees Muse's simplicity as its biggest draw. The assistant lives in a messenger-style window, handles work quickly, and has garnered rave reviews from techie first adopters. And though it's meant to handle work, it also answers questions, like ChatGPT.

Instinct, similarly, leans into ease of use as a selling point — you don't need to download an app. You just text it.

If the tools continue their boom in popularity, they could eat into OpenAI's attempt to make it a one-stop shop for work.

OpenAI's response could arrive within days

Shah expects OpenAI to launch something similar to Muse and Instinct.

And on Monday, the Information reported that OpenAI is developing features to compete with the new AI assistant apps. We could see the response very soon. Altman wrote on X that he's excited for something big to ship next week, when OpenAI holds its yearly DevDay conference.

Shah said that in this still-early stage of AI competition, she assumes no top company wants to be left out of any popular market. She said that despite Muse's speedy growth, the contest is far from over since retention indicates success better than the early wave of downloads.

"Even within the chatbots, there are different levels of engagement, different levels of churn, different levels of retention," Shah said. "And ChatGPT is the most successful in those metrics at the moment."

text:
Microsoft introduced an updated version of its Copilot app on Friday, combining AI chat, coding tools, and autonomous agents into a single product as the company tries to expand adoption among business customers and counter competition from Anthropic and OpenAI.

The new app is organized around three sections. Home brings together conversational chat and a task-delegation feature called Cowork, and also embeds full versions of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint so users can create and edit documents without leaving Copilot. Code allows non-technical users to build apps, dashboards, and automations by describing them in plain language, using the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot. Autopilot, previously called Scout, lets users create always-on agents that run in the cloud, monitor email and Teams channels, and carry out recurring tasks without waiting for a new prompt, the company said.

Microsoft has sold its 365 Copilot AI assistant and its GitHub Copilot coding agent as separate products. The new app combines those functions in a single experience. Fewer than 7% of more than 450 million commercial Microsoft 365 seats carry Copilot licenses, according to CNBC. Microsoft reported more than 30 million paid Copilot seats in July.

The launch also comes with a pricing shift. A monthly per-user license keeps covering standard functions — chat and the Copilot capabilities built into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams — while Cowork, Code, and Autopilot will be metered by consumption, as will the newest frontier models, the company said. Microsoft Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella told investors in July that the company is moving "beyond per-seat to per-seat-plus-consumption," according to GeekWire.

Jacob Andreou, Microsoft's executive vice president for Copilot, told CNBC that the company is "holding a very high bar" and that the product performs best when it focuses on delivering value and quality to users. He acknowledged that adding coding to the app represents an instance of Microsoft playing catch-up, according to CNBC.

Copilot continues to draw on models from OpenAI and Anthropic alongside Microsoft's own. Within the coding product, users can choose from several models, including one from Microsoft, though no Microsoft model appears among the options in the Home tab, according to CNBC.

text:
Scott Wilson knows what it is like to make a contrarian bet that pays off big. His early investment in SpaceX helped create a multi-billion dollar windfall for Washington University's endowment.

Now he's making another one: The trillion-dollar AI labs are in major trouble.

Wilson argues that OpenAI and Anthropic have committed to enormous spending just as cheaper Chinese models are catching up. It's a view that puts him squarely at odds with AI bulls like Vinod Khosla, who believes those massive infrastructure investments are precisely what will make the frontier labs hard to beat.

"These trillion-dollar-plus frontier companies are not worth the liabilities that they signed up for," Wilson said. "There's going to be a ton of free alternatives."

OpenAI has returned huge markups for VC firms as well as schools such as the University of Michigan, whose early $20 million OpenAI investment is now worth over $2 billion. Wilson said he also had the chance to be an early investor in OpenAI but passed because he was not convinced the company would ever make money. Since then, his bearish view has hardened.

"When we looked at the original OpenAI deal that some of our peers participated in and made tons of money on paper, we were highly skeptical," Wilson said. "I've gotten more skeptical over time."

Wilson shared what he called his "unpopular opinion" onstage last week at Rock Yard Roundup, a Fort Worth gathering of roughly 100 asset managers, VCs, and tech founders. Between a honky-tonk crawl and a visit to the Stockyards Rodeo, he cast the frontier AI race as its own kind of Wild West: a frenzy of runaway spending and valuations that, in his view, is unlikely to end well.

Wilson's warning comes as Chinese model makers such as DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen, Zhipu AI, and Tencent have narrowed the gap with U.S. frontier labs on performance while offering major cost savings. That has fueled a broader investor debate over whether OpenAI and Anthropic, which is expected to go public next month, can sustain the enormous spending required to stay ahead if customers can switch to cheaper alternatives that are almost as good.

Wilson explained that he has become more dubious about frontier labs after talking to his colleagues on the ground in China, who have seen rapid progress in open-weight models. He grew more concerned after speaking with the founders of companies Washington University has invested in, who told him they were all switching to cheaper models.

"Whenever we talk to our portfolio companies, especially the ones who are heavy of AI, they are all moving aggressively towards open source," he said. "It's like any other high-cost U.S. good that has to compete with a low-cost import, particularly from China."

Khosla says he's never been more bullish on OpenAI

Data from OpenRouter, a platform where developers route requests among AI models, supports Wilson's argument, though it is a limited snapshot. DeepSeek accounts for 25.3% of text-model requests on OpenRouter compared with 18.6% for OpenAI and 2.9% for Anthropic.

Khosla, a billionaire venture investor who was an early investor in OpenAI, told Business Insider he strongly disagrees with Wilson and said he has never been more bullish on OpenAI.

"People like that are silly, and they don't understand how this works," he said when told of Wilson's view. "They have this notion that the model is the value."

Khosla argued that the real advantage lies in controlling more of the expensive infrastructure beneath the model. A closed-model company can co-design chips, as OpenAI has done with its Jalapeño inference chip, around its own models and serving systems. That could reduce its reliance on Nvidia hardware and third-party cloud services, he said, lowering its cost to serve customers relative to an open-weight model run on someone else's cloud.

"I'm not talking price, I'm talking about cost," he said. "From power to data center to chips, to infrastructure software to inference models, the cost of the stack is almost certainly going to be lower in closed-source models than open-source."
